The story of "Two Friends" is set parallel to the events of the original Dustwind campaign ("The Last Resort"). You and your friend Bob live a quiet, boring life as scavengers. notes.title: Dustwind : Two Friends (Mini) Campaign News
notes.notes:
Hello there, post-apocalyptic warriors!
 
We are finalizing the new (mini) campaign and are looking forward to release it in the near future. 
We'd like to share some information about the upcoming release of the mini-campaign. It's going to be more concentrated on new characters and storyline, while maintaining our solid gameplay, based on the main title. So, as many of you liked the game mechanics of Dustwind, we really hope that you'll enjoy this new batch of content. All the main components, which make a game fun, are in place. If it's the very first time for you to play the game, then it can be even more fascinating as you get acquainted with the characters and the whole pack of the story.
 
Besides, we've concentrated on your feedback, smoothing out rough edges and adding elements that can enhance gameplay engagement. Eventually the basic idea was to improve the singleplayer experience at this stage of the project evolution. Although the campaign is not very long, the newly added storyline's twists and turns will hopefully make it more exciting and enjoyable to play. 
Very soon you'll be able to collect weapons and gear, choose your character based on your gameplay preferences and, as it was ever before, become a leading figure in these dark times!
 
Additionally to the new content we also did some improvements for the editor.

We are looking forward to release the free update with the new campaing.


Truly yours,
Z-Software team

notes.title: The Show Must Go On?
notes.notes:
It seems that the post-apocalyptic theme in mass culture never gets old, and has even a kind of revival lately. It was exciting to have a glance at [i]"Fallout" [/i] film adaptation and lots of people are looking forward to watch the premiere of [i]"Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga"[/i].
 
The whole thing inspired us to think over the possible extension for the storyline of Dustwind!
 
As you know, many years have passed in the game world since the catastrophic event in which an artificial intelligence called the Mainframe has gone rogue and turned it's robotic armies against all other lifeforms on Earth.
 
But even if you familiar with the main heroine series of adventures of the [b][i]"Last Resort"[/i][/b] campaign, haven't you been curious to immerse deeper into the dystopian lore?
 
Anyway, we need your help, survivors! Just let us know, that you're interested in the evolving of the storyline by hitting "Like" button: let's aim for 100, for example. If we collect enough of your reactions and feedback, then we'll definitely be more charged to release new content for the game!
 
Share your opinions in the commentaries, what do you guys like more, when this or that franchise continue its way: should it be sequel, prequel or spin-off?
 
[b][i]Keep in touch and stay tuned![/i][/b]

Changelog:

[*] Added a water tile
[*] Added new ‘Take vehicles’ flag to location change scripts so vehicles don’t get left behind in campaigns
[*] Added the ability to include custom audio files in campaigns
[*] Added voice acting support. Refer to the editor manual for details!
[*] Added scripts for playing custom music and sound effects
[*] Added ‘Clear’ button to script debug log
[*] Added recruit unlock objective feature, allowing you to add/remove recruits via objectives in campaigns
[*] Added ‘UnitSeenBy’ script trigger
[*] Added some new script conditions: ‘IsVehicle’, ‘IsTimerFinished’, ‘CheckZoneEnabled’, ‘CheckEntityEnabled’, ‘CheckUnitIsInSquad’, ‘CheckTeamRelation’, ‘CheckUnitSeenBy’

[*] Fixed some bugs when custom items are deleted

[*] Fixed ragdolls not properly handling zone enter/exit events
[*] Fixed the numbering on tasks in the PDA

notes.title: The Fallout Tactics-inspired Dustwind blasts out of early access
notes.notes:
I’ve always thought that Fallout Tactics got an unfairly bad rap. Yes, it had its balance and structure issues, but it had an interesting combat engine. I’d like to think that Dustwind‘s developers agree, as their game bears more than a passing resemblance. Fraser Brown took a look at it while it was in early access, and found an intriguing web of systems, sadly under-populated. With the release of the full version yesterday that seems less of an issue, as it now includes solo squad command (real-time with pause style) and a bevy of co-op modes, user-made solo missions and bots.

Coming back to you right from the wasteland with a TON of bigger & smaller fixes and improvements in this May update! 
Here are some highlights:

- Added Incapacitation mechanic with an “Instant Death” server setting. When turned off, units will become incapacitated instead of dying immediately and can be revived by healing. By default, Instant Death is turned ON on PvP, and turned OFF on PvE.

- If a unit runs into a sneaking enemy, both will fall on their butts and the sneaking unit(s) will lose sneak.

- Added even more environment assets

- Re-worked pathfinding to improve overall stability & reduce the ammount of times characters get stuck in a wall & similar problems. Also baking a navmesh in the Map Editor is no longer required, a navmesh will be generated at map load automatically. 

Important note for mappers: since the updated pathfinding system is not identic with the old one, we advise you to check the paths on your maps (especially in tighter spots) with the updated system.

- Updated turrets: they no longer rotate when idle (better performance), and they now have a limited firing angle (more tactical  gameplay).

notes.title: Premature Evaluation: Dustwind
notes.notes:
This week s Premature Evaluation dumps Fraser in Dustwind s isometric wasteland, forced to murder other players in grisly real-time tactical brawls. Also it has dogs.

I’ll admit it — I decided to take Dustwind for a spin primarily because of one line on the Steam store page: Play as a dog. In post-apocalyptic battle arenas that evoke Fallout and Wasteland, no less. And we re not talking about your run-of-the-mill, hangs out in dog parks defecating everywhere kind of dog. No, Dustwind s pooches are battle-hardened terrors, capable of covering the battlefield in mines or manning a vehicle s turret. How could I say no? How could it go wrong?
